t: #3081 Replace Question Marks in String to Minimize Its Value
o: **Understanding the problem**: Fixed letters contribute a constant cost Σ C(freq(c), 2). Each '?' must be filled with a letter; filling letter c when it already occurs f times adds f to the total cost (each new copy pairs with every existing copy). So we must choose a multiset of q letters minimizing Σ [C(f_c + a_c, 2) − C(f_c, 2)], and then place them lexicographically smallest. Example: "???" → one each of a,b,c gives cost 0; "a?a?" → add b and c giving "abac" with cost 1.
k: Cost is separable per letter and convex in the count, so the optimal fill balances final frequencies (greedy: always increment the currently least-frequent letter).
Lexicographic tie-break: sort the chosen letters ascending and drop them into the '?' positions left to right — placement order never affects cost.

a.i: Push all 26 letters keyed by current frequency; pop the least-frequent (smallest letter on ties) q times, recording each pick. Convexity of C(f,2) guarantees this yields the minimum total cost.
s: Count fixed-letter frequencies; build a min-heap of (freq, letter).
Pop q times, appending the picked letter and pushing back (freq+1, letter).
Sort the picked letters ascending and substitute them into the '?' positions in order.

c.python:
import heapq
from collections import Counter
import string

class Solution:
    def minimizeStringValue(self, s: str) -> str:
        cnt = Counter(ch for ch in s if ch != '?')
        heap = [(cnt[ch], ch) for ch in string.ascii_lowercase]
        heapq.heapify(heap)
        add = []
        for _ in range(s.count('?')):
            f, ch = heapq.heappop(heap)
            add.append(ch)
            heapq.heappush(heap, (f + 1, ch))
        add.sort()
        it = iter(add)
        return ''.join(next(it) if ch == '?' else ch for ch in s)

a.t: O(n + q log 26 + q log q) — counting, q heap ops on a 26-element heap, final sort of q letters

a.i: Because the optimum balances counts, sort the 26 letters by current frequency; with q fills, every letter gets ⌊q/26⌋ extra copies and the q mod 26 least-frequent letters get one more. This computes the exact multiset in one sort, then fills as before.
s: Count frequencies; create letter indices sorted by (freq, letter).
Assign base = q // 26 extra copies to everyone, plus 1 to the first q % 26 letters in sorted order.
Expand into a sorted multiset of letters and substitute into '?' positions.
a.t: O(n + 26 log 26 + q log q) — dominated by counting and the final sort of added letters

w: **Wrap-up**: Lead with the heap version — the greedy "always bump the rarest letter" is easy to justify via exchange argument on the convex cost. Pitfalls: placing letters into '?' positions in sorted order (not heap-pop order) for the lexicographic requirement, and remembering fixed letters' costs are unavoidable so only the added copies matter. Follow-ups: maximize the value instead (give all '?' the same most-frequent letter), or forbid certain letters.
